selected.name: Poses an explicit or implicit question
selected.instruction: Scores high if the syntax forms a direct question, uses scare quotes to challenge a concept, or teases a hidden explanation. Scores low if the headline is a declarative statement of fact.
selected.rationale: Information gaps provoke high curiosity, driving readers to click to resolve the mystery.
member_names: Poses an explicit or implicit question

selected.name: Visual scene vividness
selected.instruction: Scores high when the wording readily evokes a specific, imaginable scene, and low when it remains abstract; does not apply when no concrete scene is described.
selected.rationale: Easily imagined scenes make headlines more attention-grabbing and memorable.

selected.name: Everyday-Life Relevance
selected.instruction: high when readers can map the story to ordinary routines, safety, money, family, or identity; low when it is remote or specialized. Does not apply when the headline offers no basis for judging relevance
selected.rationale: Everyday relevance can attract readers independently of conventional news values.

selected.name: Emotional arousal
selected.instruction: High when wording clearly evokes strong fear, anger, joy, disgust, or awe; low when emotionally neutral, and it does not apply when no affective response is signaled. | DESCRIPTION: Emotional intensity is separate from crisis, violence, or human-interest content.
selected.rationale: Strong affect can prompt impulsive attention and clicking.

selected.name: Conversation Potential
selected.instruction: high when the headline invites broad opinion, argument, empathy, or emotional reaction; low when it offers no social or evaluative angle. Does not apply without a proposition likely to prompt response
selected.rationale: Discussion potential can amplify readership through disagreement, empathy, or social sharing.

selected.name: Practical Utility
selected.instruction: high when reading promises guidance for a decision, behavior, or situation; low when no action follows. Does not apply to purely descriptive stories with no implied decision
selected.rationale: Actionable information gives readers a direct instrumental reason to open the article.

selected.name: Plain-language accessibility
selected.instruction: High when common words and straightforward syntax make the meaning instantly clear; low when jargon or dense construction impedes comprehension, and it does not apply when unavoidable technical language is central. | DESCRIPTION: Accessible phrasing expands the pool of readers who can understand the headline immediately.
selected.rationale: Comprehension is a prerequisite for broad readership and clicking.

selected.name: Perceived Contradiction
selected.instruction: high when the headline juxtaposes roles, expectations, or facts that seem incompatible; low when elements reinforce one another. Does not apply without a readable contrast
selected.rationale: Contradiction creates a cognitive puzzle that can motivate opening the story.

selected.name: Moral contestability
selected.instruction: Scores high when the headline invites judgment about right, wrong, fairness, or responsibility, and low when no normative evaluation is suggested; does not apply to normatively neutral events.
selected.rationale: Moral evaluation can generate readership through disagreement and self-positioning.

selected.name: Emotional Trigger Words
selected.instruction: Headlines containing visceral emotional adjectives (e.g., 'worst', 'unbearable', 'anger') score 1; purely factual headlines score 0. Does not apply to neutral headlines.
selected.rationale: Strong emotive language taps into affective responses that drive high click-through rates.

selected.name: Quoted first-person speech
selected.instruction: Headline contains text in quotation marks spoken by an everyday individual expressing a subjective feeling or personal experience; low for unquoted statements.
selected.rationale: First-person quotes simulate emotional intimacy and voyeurism, directly engaging readers.

selected.name: Concrete specificity
selected.instruction: High when the headline supplies precise, distinctive details rather than generic abstractions; low when vague, and it does not apply when the subject cannot be described more specifically. | DESCRIPTION: Specific wording helps readers form an immediate mental model of the article.
selected.rationale: Concrete titles reduce uncertainty about what clicking will deliver.

selected.name: UK-centric cultural or local hook
selected.instruction: Scores high if mentioning UK entities (e.g., Wetherspoons); scores low for foreign equivalents without domestic ties.
selected.rationale: BBC's primarily domestic audience clicks heavily on hyper-local or culturally familiar soft news.

selected.name: Identity resonance
selected.instruction: High when the headline invokes belonging, values, language, generation, or group experience; low when no identity cue appears, and it does not apply when identity is merely incidental. | DESCRIPTION: Identity-linked material may feel personally significant to readers.
selected.rationale: Group identification can increase attention and perceived self-relevance.

selected.name: Credibility Framing
selected.instruction: high when a claim is attributed to an identifiable source or grounded in concrete evidence; low when unsupported or sensationalized. Does not apply to straightforward event reports
selected.rationale: Attribution and evidence cues affect trust and willingness to investigate a claim.

selected.name: Question/explainer framing
selected.instruction: <=8 words | DESCRIPTION: Mark headlines that are questions or begin with “why,” “how,” or “can.”
upstream_parent_all_members: Editorial placement in designated click-magnet slots or soft-news promotional pushes
explainer format slot and homepage packaging

selected.name: Scare-quoted hook
selected.instruction: Places a colloquial, evaluative, or slogan-like phrase in quotation marks rather than using only plain event wording.
upstream_parent_all_members: House-style formatting for optimized reader-engagement features and explainers
house style or CMS formatting habit

selected.name: Headline length
selected.instruction: <=8 words | DESCRIPTION: Count the headline’s whitespace-delimited words, ignoring punctuation. Treat unusually short or long headlines as the channel.

selected.name: First-person testimony
selected.instruction: Mark headlines using “I”, “my”, or an individualized first-person account.

selected.name: Continuation or ordinal cue
selected.instruction: Headline uses words such as “second,” “again,” “back,” “after,” or “now” to signal a follow-up.
selected.upstream_parent: multi-day running story and sequence position
upstream_parent_all_members: multi-day running story and sequence position
position in a running story or package

selected.name: Obituary-label template
selected.instruction: Headline explicitly starts with “Obituary:” or uses a death-and-age formula.
selected.upstream_parent: obituary desk template and staffing workflow
upstream_parent_all_members: obituary desk template and staffing workflow

selected.name: Explicit extreme emotion label
selected.instruction: Headline uses overt emotional or evaluative words to describe the situation, such as 'disaster', 'catastrophe', 'unbearable', 'tricky', or 'anger'.

selected.name: DOMESTIC-VS-FOREIGN-SYNTAX
selected.instruction: Headline follows terse, immediate syntax for domestic/visual events (e.g., "Russian jet shot down") but uses summarizing syntax for foreign events (e.g., "Chad army snubs...").
selected.upstream_parent: Proximity bias and varying editorial desk resources between domestic and foreign beats
upstream_parent_all_members: Proximity bias and varying editorial desk resources between domestic and foreign beats

selected.name: CELEBRITY OBITUARY
selected.instruction: Names deceased famous person | DESCRIPTION: Headline explicitly mentions the death of an actor, musician, or public entertainer, triggering immediate high-volume reader searches.
upstream_parent_all_members: Rapid editorial mobilization for pre-written, highly anticipated celebrity deaths

selected.name: Numeral milestone wording
selected.instruction: Headline includes a specific number tied to a count, age, date, term, or measured milestone.

A.rule: FREEZE DECLARATION identity rule -- concept identity by full-recall blind pairwise adjudication, never embedding-tau. The cosine only shortlisted candidate pairs (cross-proposer pairs at cos >= 0.55).
